strings.hub.biblical.title: Biblical Characters
strings.hub.biblical.subtitle: The people of Sacred Scripture
strings.hub.biblical.intro: From the first man in the garden to the apostles of the Church, the Bible tells its story through people—called, tested, and remembered. Here are the great figures of Scripture and who they were.
strings.sec.biblical.beginning.title: In the Beginning
strings.sec.biblical.beginning.summary: The first family and the world before the Flood.
strings.art.biblical.beginning.title: In the Beginning
strings.art.biblical.beginning.lead: The first family and the world before the Flood.
strings.fig.adam.name: Adam
strings.fig.adam.desc: The first man, formed by God from the dust of the earth and given dominion over creation. Through his disobedience in Eden sin entered the world, and the Church honours Christ as the “new Adam” who undoes his fall.
strings.fig.eve.name: Eve
strings.fig.eve.desc: The first woman, drawn from Adam's side and named “mother of all the living.” Tempted by the serpent, she and Adam ate the forbidden fruit; tradition sees Mary as the “new Eve” whose obedience answers hers.
strings.fig.cain.name: Cain
strings.fig.cain.desc: The firstborn son of Adam and Eve, a tiller of the soil. In jealousy over God's favour he murdered his brother Abel, becoming Scripture's first killer and a wanderer marked by God.
strings.fig.abel.name: Abel
strings.fig.abel.desc: The second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of flocks whose offering pleased God. Slain by his brother Cain, he is remembered as the first martyr, his innocent blood crying out from the ground.
strings.fig.seth.name: Seth
strings.fig.seth.desc: The third son of Adam and Eve, born after Abel's death and Cain's exile. Through his line the faithful worship of God was carried on down to Noah.
strings.fig.enoch.name: Enoch
strings.fig.enoch.desc: A man who “walked with God” and did not see death, for God took him up. His unbroken closeness to God made him a sign of hope beyond the grave.
strings.fig.noah.name: Noah
strings.fig.noah.desc: A righteous man in a corrupt age, commanded by God to build an ark and save his family and the animals from the Flood. God's covenant with him, sealed by the rainbow, promised never again to destroy the earth by water.
strings.sec.biblical.patriarchs.title: The Patriarchs
strings.sec.biblical.patriarchs.summary: Abraham and the fathers of God's chosen people.
strings.art.biblical.patriarchs.title: The Patriarchs
strings.art.biblical.patriarchs.lead: Abraham and the fathers of God's chosen people.
strings.fig.abraham.name: Abraham
strings.fig.abraham.desc: Called by God from Ur, he left his homeland on a promise and became the father of a great nation and “father of all who believe.” His readiness to sacrifice his son Isaac is the model of faith and obedience.
strings.fig.sarah.name: Sarah
strings.fig.sarah.desc: The wife of Abraham, long barren, who laughed when told she would bear a child in old age. God kept his word, and she became the mother of Isaac and matriarch of the people of promise.
strings.fig.hagar.name: Hagar
strings.fig.hagar.desc: The Egyptian servant of Sarah and mother of Ishmael by Abraham. Cast into the desert, she was met by an angel at a well and promised that her son would father a great people.
strings.fig.ishmael.name: Ishmael
strings.fig.ishmael.desc: The firstborn son of Abraham by Hagar. Though the covenant passed to Isaac, God blessed Ishmael and made of him a great nation.
strings.fig.lot.name: Lot
strings.fig.lot.desc: The nephew of Abraham who settled in Sodom and was rescued by angels before the city's destruction. Warned not to look back, his wife turned and became a pillar of salt.
strings.fig.melchizedek.name: Melchizedek
strings.fig.melchizedek.desc: The mysterious king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham and offered bread and wine. The Church sees in him a foreshadowing of Christ's eternal priesthood.
strings.fig.isaac.name: Isaac
strings.fig.isaac.desc: The son of Abraham and Sarah, child of the promise, spared on Mount Moriah when God provided a ram in his place. Through his son Jacob the covenant passed to the twelve tribes of Israel.
strings.fig.rebekah.name: Rebekah
strings.fig.rebekah.desc: The wife of Isaac, met at a well and chosen for her kindness. Mother of the twins Esau and Jacob, she helped secure the birthright and blessing for her younger son.
strings.fig.esau.name: Esau
strings.fig.esau.desc: The elder twin of Jacob, a hunter who sold his birthright for a bowl of stew and lost his father's blessing. Though wronged, he later reconciled with his brother.
strings.fig.jacob.name: Jacob
strings.fig.jacob.desc: Son of Isaac, who wrestled with an angel and was renamed Israel. Father of twelve sons whose descendants became the twelve tribes, he is a pillar of the patriarchal line.
strings.fig.rachel.name: Rachel
strings.fig.rachel.desc: The beloved wife of Jacob, for whom he laboured fourteen years. Mother of Joseph and Benjamin, she died in childbirth and was long mourned as a mother weeping for her children.
strings.fig.leah.name: Leah
strings.fig.leah.desc: The elder daughter of Laban and first wife of Jacob, long unloved yet fruitful. Mother of six of the twelve tribes, including Judah and Levi, from whom kings and priests would come.
strings.fig.joseph_egypt.name: Joseph
strings.fig.joseph_egypt.desc: The favoured son of Jacob, sold into slavery in Egypt by his jealous brothers. Rising to govern the land through his gift for interpreting dreams, he saved his family from famine and forgave those who had wronged him.
strings.fig.judah.name: Judah
strings.fig.judah.desc: The fourth son of Jacob and Leah, who pledged his own life for his brother Benjamin. From his tribe came King David and, in the fullness of time, the Messiah—the Lion of Judah.
strings.sec.biblical.exodus.title: Exodus & the Law
strings.sec.biblical.exodus.summary: Moses and the deliverance of Israel from Egypt.
strings.art.biblical.exodus.title: Exodus & the Law
strings.art.biblical.exodus.lead: Moses and the deliverance of Israel from Egypt.
strings.fig.moses.name: Moses
strings.fig.moses.desc: Drawn from the Nile as an infant and raised in Pharaoh's house, he was called at the burning bush to lead Israel out of slavery. Through him God parted the sea and gave the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai.
strings.fig.aaron.name: Aaron
strings.fig.aaron.desc: The elder brother of Moses and his spokesman before Pharaoh. Consecrated as the first high priest of Israel, he ministered at the altar, though he also fashioned the golden calf in the people's rebellion.
strings.fig.miriam.name: Miriam
strings.fig.miriam.desc: The sister of Moses and Aaron, who watched over him in the bulrushes. A prophetess, she led the women in song and dance after the crossing of the sea.
strings.fig.joshua.name: Joshua
strings.fig.joshua.desc: The successor of Moses who led Israel across the Jordan into the Promised Land. At his command the walls of Jericho fell, and he divided the land among the tribes.
strings.fig.caleb.name: Caleb
strings.fig.caleb.desc: One of the twelve spies sent into Canaan, who with Joshua alone trusted God's promise. For his faith he was allowed to enter the Promised Land and given Hebron as his inheritance.
strings.fig.balaam.name: Balaam
strings.fig.balaam.desc: A pagan seer hired to curse Israel, whose donkey saw the angel of the Lord and spoke to rebuke him. Unable to curse, he blessed God's people instead and foretold a star rising out of Jacob.
strings.sec.biblical.judges_kings.title: Judges & Kings
strings.sec.biblical.judges_kings.summary: The champions, judges and kings of ancient Israel.
strings.art.biblical.judges_kings.title: Judges & Kings
strings.art.biblical.judges_kings.lead: The champions, judges and kings of ancient Israel.
strings.fig.deborah.name: Deborah
strings.fig.deborah.desc: A prophetess and the only woman among the judges of Israel. She summoned Barak to battle and led the people to victory over their oppressors, celebrated in one of Scripture's oldest songs.
strings.fig.gideon.name: Gideon
strings.fig.gideon.desc: A reluctant judge called by an angel to deliver Israel from Midian. With only three hundred men and torches hidden in jars, he routed a vast army by the power of God.
strings.fig.samson.name: Samson
strings.fig.samson.desc: A judge of prodigious strength, consecrated to God as a Nazirite from birth. Betrayed by Delilah, who cut his hair, he brought down the temple of the Philistines in his final act.
strings.fig.ruth.name: Ruth
strings.fig.ruth.desc: A Moabite widow whose loyalty to her mother-in-law Naomi brought her to Bethlehem. Married to Boaz, she became the great-grandmother of King David and an ancestor of Christ.
strings.fig.boaz.name: Boaz
strings.fig.boaz.desc: A wealthy and upright landowner of Bethlehem who showed kindness to the widow Ruth and married her as her kinsman-redeemer. Their union placed him in the ancestry of King David and of Christ.
strings.fig.samuel.name: Samuel
strings.fig.samuel.desc: The last of the judges and a great prophet, given to God's service as a child. He anointed both Saul and David as the first kings of Israel.
strings.fig.saul.name: Saul
strings.fig.saul.desc: The first king of Israel, chosen and anointed by Samuel. Tall and valiant at first, his disobedience and jealousy of David cost him God's favour and his throne.
strings.fig.david.name: David
strings.fig.david.desc: The shepherd boy anointed king, a man after God's own heart. Slayer of Goliath, singer of the Psalms and founder of Jerusalem's royal line, he is the ancestor from whom the Messiah would come.
strings.fig.jonathan.name: Jonathan
strings.fig.jonathan.desc: The son of King Saul and the devoted friend of David, whose loyalty outweighed his own claim to the throne. He fell with his father in battle against the Philistines.
strings.fig.goliath.name: Goliath
strings.fig.goliath.desc: The giant Philistine champion who defied the armies of Israel. He was felled by the young David with a single stone from a sling, a lasting emblem of faith overcoming brute strength.
strings.fig.solomon.name: Solomon
strings.fig.solomon.desc: The son of David, renowned for the wisdom God granted him. He built the great Temple in Jerusalem, though his later idolatry divided the kingdom after his death.
strings.fig.absalom.name: Absalom
strings.fig.absalom.desc: The handsome and ambitious son of David who rose in rebellion against his father. Fleeing on a mule, his long hair caught in an oak, and he was killed—David's grief for him is famous.
strings.fig.jezebel.name: Jezebel
strings.fig.jezebel.desc: The foreign queen of King Ahab who promoted the worship of Baal and persecuted the prophets of God. Denounced by Elijah, her violent end became a byword for wickedness and idolatry.
strings.fig.ahab.name: Ahab
strings.fig.ahab.desc: A king of Israel who, led by his wife Jezebel, gave himself to the worship of Baal. Rebuked by Elijah and defeated in battle, his reign became a warning against idolatry.
strings.fig.jesse.name: Jesse
strings.fig.jesse.desc: The father of King David, of Bethlehem, from whose family the Messiah would spring. Isaiah foretold a shoot springing from the stump of Jesse, a favourite image of Christ's royal descent.
strings.fig.hezekiah.name: Hezekiah
strings.fig.hezekiah.desc: A faithful king of Judah who tore down idols and trusted God when Jerusalem was besieged. His fervent prayer was answered, and his life was lengthened by fifteen years.
strings.fig.josiah.name: Josiah
strings.fig.josiah.desc: A young king of Judah who rediscovered the lost Book of the Law and led a great renewal, purging idolatry and restoring the true worship of God.
strings.fig.mordecai.name: Mordecai
strings.fig.mordecai.desc: A devout Jew of the Persian court, cousin and guardian of Queen Esther. His refusal to bow and his counsel to her helped save his people from destruction.
strings.fig.haman.name: Haman
strings.fig.haman.desc: The proud royal minister of Persia who plotted to destroy the Jews, enraged that Mordecai would not bow to him. His scheme recoiled upon himself, and he perished on the gallows he had built.
strings.sec.biblical.prophets.title: The Prophets
strings.sec.biblical.prophets.summary: The voices God raised to call his people back.
strings.art.biblical.prophets.title: The Prophets
strings.art.biblical.prophets.lead: The voices God raised to call his people back.
strings.fig.elijah.name: Elijah
strings.fig.elijah.desc: A fiery prophet who confronted the priests of Baal on Mount Carmel and was fed by ravens in the wilderness. Taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire, he appears again at Christ's Transfiguration.
strings.fig.elisha.name: Elisha
strings.fig.elisha.desc: The disciple and successor of Elijah, who received a double share of his spirit. His ministry was marked by many miracles of healing and provision among the people.
strings.fig.isaiah.name: Isaiah
strings.fig.isaiah.desc: The prophet of the Messiah, who foretold a virgin bearing a son called Emmanuel and the suffering servant who bears our sins. His visions of God's holiness shaped Israel's hope.
strings.fig.jeremiah.name: Jeremiah
strings.fig.jeremiah.desc: The “weeping prophet” who warned Jerusalem of its fall and suffered greatly for his message. He promised a new covenant written on the human heart.
strings.fig.ezekiel.name: Ezekiel
strings.fig.ezekiel.desc: A priest exiled to Babylon and called to prophesy in vivid visions—the wheels of fire, the valley of dry bones brought to life. He promised his people a new heart and a new spirit.
strings.fig.nathan.name: Nathan
strings.fig.nathan.desc: The court prophet who confronted King David over his sin with a parable that pierced his conscience. He also delivered God's promise of an everlasting throne to David's house.
strings.fig.daniel.name: Daniel
strings.fig.daniel.desc: A young exile in Babylon, faithful to God amid a pagan court. Delivered unharmed from the lions' den, he interpreted dreams and received visions of the kingdoms to come.
strings.fig.jonah.name: Jonah
strings.fig.jonah.desc: The prophet who fled God's call and was swallowed by a great fish for three days. Delivered, he preached to Nineveh, which repented—a sign Christ applied to his own resurrection.
strings.fig.job.name: Job
strings.fig.job.desc: A blameless man stripped of his wealth, children and health, tested to the limit of endurance. Refusing to curse God, he questioned his suffering and was answered out of the whirlwind, then restored.
strings.fig.hosea.name: Hosea
strings.fig.hosea.desc: A prophet commanded to marry an unfaithful wife as a living image of Israel's betrayal of God—and of the Lord's unbreakable, forgiving love that always calls his people home.
strings.fig.amos.name: Amos
strings.fig.amos.desc: A shepherd from Tekoa called to prophesy against injustice and empty worship. He thundered that God desires righteousness to “roll down like waters,” not mere sacrifice.
strings.fig.ezra.name: Ezra
strings.fig.ezra.desc: A priest and scribe who led exiles back from Babylon and restored the Law of Moses among the people. He read the Scriptures aloud to the assembly and renewed the covenant.
strings.fig.nehemiah.name: Nehemiah
strings.fig.nehemiah.desc: A cupbearer to the Persian king who returned to rebuild the ruined walls of Jerusalem despite fierce opposition. His faith and resolve restored the holy city.
strings.fig.naaman.name: Naaman
strings.fig.naaman.desc: A Syrian army commander stricken with leprosy, healed when he humbled himself to wash seven times in the Jordan at the word of the prophet Elisha.
strings.fig.nebuchadnezzar.name: Nebuchadnezzar
strings.fig.nebuchadnezzar.desc: The mighty king of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and carried Judah into exile. Humbled by God until he acknowledged the Most High, he learned that heaven rules over the proud.
strings.fig.three_hebrews.name: Shadrach, Meshach & Abednego
strings.fig.three_hebrews.desc: Three young Hebrews in Babylon who refused to worship the king's golden image and were cast into a blazing furnace. They walked unharmed in the flames, a fourth figure at their side, and came out untouched.
strings.sec.biblical.women.title: Women of Faith
strings.sec.biblical.women.summary: Heroines whose courage saved God's people.
strings.art.biblical.women.title: Women of Faith
strings.art.biblical.women.lead: Heroines whose courage saved God's people.
strings.fig.hannah.name: Hannah
strings.fig.hannah.desc: A woman who prayed through her tears for a child and vowed to give him to God. Her prayer answered, she brought her son Samuel to the sanctuary, and her canticle prefigures Mary's Magnificat.
strings.fig.esther.name: Esther
strings.fig.esther.desc: A Jewish orphan who became queen of Persia and risked her life to expose a plot against her people. “For such a time as this,” she interceded before the king and saved the Jews from destruction.
strings.fig.judith.name: Judith
strings.fig.judith.desc: A devout widow who saved her besieged city by boldly entering the enemy camp and beheading the general Holofernes. Her courage is celebrated as the deliverance of her people.
strings.fig.rahab.name: Rahab
strings.fig.rahab.desc: A woman of Jericho who hid Joshua's spies and was spared when the city fell. Named among the ancestors of Christ, she is praised for her faith.
strings.fig.naomi.name: Naomi
strings.fig.naomi.desc: The widow of Bethlehem who lost her husband and sons in Moab and returned home in bitterness. The devotion of her daughter-in-law Ruth restored her, and she cradled the grandfather of King David.
strings.fig.bathsheba.name: Bathsheba
strings.fig.bathsheba.desc: The wife of Uriah, taken by David in the great sin of his reign. She became the mother of Solomon and, as queen mother, secured his succession.
strings.fig.delilah.name: Delilah
strings.fig.delilah.desc: The Philistine woman who lured Samson into revealing that his strength lay in his uncut hair, then betrayed him to his enemies for silver.
strings.sec.biblical.new_testament.title: The New Testament
strings.sec.biblical.new_testament.summary: The chief figures around the birth of the Church.
strings.art.biblical.new_testament.title: The New Testament
strings.art.biblical.new_testament.lead: The chief figures around the birth of the Church.
strings.fig.jesus.name: Jesus Christ
strings.fig.jesus.desc: The Son of God made man, born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem. He preached the Kingdom, worked signs and wonders, and by his death on the Cross and resurrection redeemed the world—the promised Messiah and the heart of all Scripture.
strings.fig.john_baptist.name: John the Baptist
strings.fig.john_baptist.desc: The forerunner who preached repentance in the wilderness and baptised Jesus in the Jordan. “The voice of one crying out,” he pointed to Christ as the Lamb of God and was beheaded by Herod.
strings.fig.zechariah.name: Zechariah
strings.fig.zechariah.desc: A priest of the Temple, husband of Elizabeth, struck mute for doubting the angel's word that they would have a son in old age. At John's birth his speech returned in a great song of praise.
strings.fig.elizabeth.name: Elizabeth
strings.fig.elizabeth.desc: The kinswoman of the Virgin Mary and mother of John the Baptist, barren until her old age. Filled with the Holy Spirit, she greeted Mary as “the mother of my Lord.”
strings.fig.mary.name: The Virgin Mary
strings.fig.mary.desc: The mother of Jesus, who answered the angel with her “yes” and bore the Son of God. Ever-virgin and full of grace, she is honoured as Mother of the Church and Queen of Heaven.
strings.fig.joseph.name: Saint Joseph
strings.fig.joseph.desc: The just man betrothed to Mary and foster-father of Jesus. A carpenter of Nazareth, he guarded the Holy Family and is venerated as patron of the universal Church and of a happy death.
strings.fig.magi.name: The Three Magi
strings.fig.magi.desc: The wise men from the East—traditionally named Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar—who followed a star to Bethlehem and knelt before the infant Jesus, offering gold, frankincense and myrrh. Their coming reveals Christ to the nations, celebrated at the Epiphany.
strings.fig.herod.name: Herod the Great
strings.fig.herod.desc: The king of Judea who, troubled by news of a newborn king, questioned the Magi and then ordered the massacre of the infants of Bethlehem. Warned in a dream, the Holy Family fled into Egypt to escape him.
strings.fig.peter.name: Saint Peter
strings.fig.peter.desc: A Galilean fisherman whom Jesus made the rock of his Church and gave the keys of the kingdom. First among the apostles, he led the early Church and was martyred in Rome.
strings.fig.andrew.name: Saint Andrew
strings.fig.andrew.desc: A fisherman and brother of Peter, one of the first called by Jesus. Tradition holds that he preached widely and was martyred on an X-shaped cross.
strings.fig.james_greater.name: Saint James
strings.fig.james_greater.desc: One of the sons of Zebedee and part of Jesus' inner circle at the Transfiguration and in Gethsemane. The first apostle to be martyred, he is venerated as the patron of pilgrims to Compostela.
strings.fig.john_evangelist.name: Saint John
strings.fig.john_evangelist.desc: The beloved disciple who leaned on Jesus at the Last Supper and stood at the foot of the Cross, to whom the Lord entrusted his Mother. He is honoured as the author of the fourth Gospel and the Book of Revelation.
strings.fig.thomas.name: Saint Thomas
strings.fig.thomas.desc: The apostle who doubted the resurrection until he touched the wounds of the risen Christ and confessed, “My Lord and my God.” Tradition sends him to preach as far as India.
strings.fig.matthew.name: Saint Matthew
strings.fig.matthew.desc: A tax collector called from his booth to follow Jesus, who left everything at a word. He is honoured as the author of the first Gospel.
strings.fig.judas_iscariot.name: Judas Iscariot
strings.fig.judas_iscariot.desc: One of the Twelve who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver with a kiss. Seized by remorse, he cast away the money and took his own life—a lasting warning against the betrayal of trust.
strings.fig.paul.name: Saint Paul
strings.fig.paul.desc: Once a persecutor of Christians, struck down and converted on the road to Damascus. The great apostle to the Gentiles, his journeys and letters carried the Gospel across the Roman world.
strings.fig.mary_magdalene.name: Mary Magdalene
strings.fig.mary_magdalene.desc: A faithful disciple healed by Christ, who stood by the Cross and came to the tomb at dawn. The first to see the risen Lord, she is called the “apostle to the apostles.”
strings.fig.lazarus.name: Lazarus
strings.fig.lazarus.desc: The brother of Martha and Mary of Bethany, raised by Jesus after four days in the tomb. His return to life foreshadowed the resurrection and hastened the plot against the Lord.
strings.fig.stephen.name: Saint Stephen
strings.fig.stephen.desc: A deacon full of grace and power, chosen to serve the poor of the early Church. The first Christian martyr, he was stoned while praying for his killers, watched over by the young Saul.
strings.fig.simeon.name: Simeon
strings.fig.simeon.desc: A devout old man promised he would not die before seeing the Messiah. Taking the child Jesus in his arms at the Temple, he sang the Nunc Dimittis and blessed him as “a light to the nations.”
strings.fig.anna.name: Anna the Prophetess
strings.fig.anna.desc: An aged prophetess who worshipped in the Temple with fasting and prayer. She saw the child Jesus at his presentation and spoke of him to all who awaited the redemption of Jerusalem.
strings.fig.nicodemus.name: Nicodemus
strings.fig.nicodemus.desc: A Pharisee and member of the council who came to Jesus by night and was told he must be “born again.” He later helped bury the Lord with myrrh and aloes.
strings.fig.zacchaeus.name: Zacchaeus
strings.fig.zacchaeus.desc: A short tax collector of Jericho who climbed a sycamore to see Jesus passing. The Lord dined at his house, and he vowed to repay fourfold all he had wronged.
strings.fig.martha.name: Martha
strings.fig.martha.desc: The sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany, who welcomed Jesus and served him. Though “anxious about many things,” she made the great confession that he is the Christ, the Son of God.
strings.fig.mary_bethany.name: Mary of Bethany
strings.fig.mary_bethany.desc: The sister of Martha and Lazarus, who sat at the feet of Jesus to listen and anointed him with costly perfume. He praised her for choosing “the better part.”
strings.fig.pilate.name: Pontius Pilate
strings.fig.pilate.desc: The Roman governor of Judea who questioned Jesus, found no guilt in him, yet handed him over to be crucified. His name endures in the Creed: “suffered under Pontius Pilate.”
strings.fig.barnabas.name: Saint Barnabas
strings.fig.barnabas.desc: A generous Levite of Cyprus who vouched for the newly converted Paul and travelled with him as a missionary. Called “son of encouragement,” he strengthened the early Church.
strings.fig.timothy.name: Saint Timothy
strings.fig.timothy.desc: A young disciple and beloved companion of Paul, entrusted with the care of the church at Ephesus. Two of Paul's letters, full of fatherly counsel, are addressed to him.
strings.fig.philip.name: Saint Philip
strings.fig.philip.desc: An apostle from Bethsaida who brought Nathanael to Jesus with the words “come and see.” At the Last Supper he asked, “Lord, show us the Father,” and was told that to see Christ is to see the Father.
strings.fig.bartholomew.name: Saint Bartholomew
strings.fig.bartholomew.desc: The apostle usually identified with Nathanael, whom Jesus praised as “a man in whom there is no guile.” Tradition holds that he preached in the East and was martyred for the faith.
strings.fig.simon_zealot.name: Saint Simon the Zealot
strings.fig.simon_zealot.desc: One of the Twelve, once numbered among the zealots ardent for Israel. Little is recorded of him, yet he is honoured among the apostles who carried the Gospel to the nations.
strings.fig.jude_thaddeus.name: Saint Jude Thaddeus
strings.fig.jude_thaddeus.desc: An apostle who asked at the Last Supper why the Lord would show himself to his own and not to the world. Venerated as the patron of desperate and hopeless causes.
strings.fig.james_lesser.name: Saint James the Less
strings.fig.james_lesser.desc: The son of Alphaeus, an apostle distinguished from James the Greater. Tradition links him to the leadership of the church in Jerusalem and to a letter bearing his name.
strings.fig.matthias.name: Saint Matthias
strings.fig.matthias.desc: The disciple chosen by lot to take the place left by Judas and restore the Twelve. Having followed Jesus from his baptism, he became a witness of the resurrection.
strings.fig.luke.name: Saint Luke
strings.fig.luke.desc: A physician and companion of Paul, author of the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles. Tradition honours him as a painter of the Virgin; his symbol is the winged ox.
strings.fig.mark.name: Saint Mark
strings.fig.mark.desc: A companion of Peter and Paul and author of the second Gospel, the shortest and most vivid. The patron of Venice, his symbol is the winged lion.
strings.fig.joseph_arimathea.name: Joseph of Arimathea
strings.fig.joseph_arimathea.desc: A rich and secret disciple, a member of the council, who boldly asked Pilate for the body of Jesus. He wrapped the Lord in linen and laid him in his own new tomb.
strings.fig.caiaphas.name: Caiaphas
strings.fig.caiaphas.desc: The high priest who presided over the council that condemned Jesus, declaring it better that one man die for the people—unknowingly prophesying the meaning of the Cross.
strings.fig.cornelius.name: Cornelius the Centurion
strings.fig.cornelius.desc: A devout Roman centurion of Caesarea whose prayers and alms were heard. Baptised by Peter with his whole household, he was the first Gentile received into the Church.
strings.fig.dismas.name: Dismas, the Good Thief
strings.fig.dismas.desc: One of the two criminals crucified beside Jesus, who rebuked the other and asked to be remembered. To him the Lord promised, “Today you will be with me in Paradise.”
strings.fig.samaritan_woman.name: The Samaritan Woman
strings.fig.samaritan_woman.desc: The woman Jesus met at Jacob's well, to whom he revealed himself as the giver of living water and the Messiah. She hurried to bring her whole town to him.
